notes.title: Dev Update & Official Discord Channel [DevInside 04]
notes.content:
[code]>> Hello Operator
MidDev here to share with you what's currently going Here's what's currently, and what's next.[/code][p][/p][h2]- Official Discord [/h2][p]The official Mech Havoc Discord channel has been created![/p][p]I'll use it to share dev updates, sneak previews and the latest news. It'll also be a place for you to ask questions, provide feedback, report problems and discuss anything related to the game.[/p][p]Join here: [url="https://discord.gg/ZzZRa6Upqq"]https://discord.gg/ZzZRa6Upqq[/url][/p][p][/p][h2]- Development Status[/h2][p]Over the past few months, I've been analyzing feedback from the demo, prioritizing features based on feasibility, how many times it was suggested, and whether it fit in the overall game design. notes.title: Demo Update 0.1.7.5
notes.content:
The first significant update to the demo since the Next Fest. Thank you everyone for playing the demo and providing feedback!

[b]Grenade distance fuze[/b]
Some weapon projectiles now have a "distance fuze", resulting in them exploding close to the point you are aiming. Allowing them to more reliably hit their their target and stack explosive AOE damage. This has been added to the following weapons:
- GL20
- GL40
- GL40 AB
- Cluster Launcher
- MRL10 (the MRL has been rebalanced in general, more on that later)
The proximity fuze of the GL40 AB is now a bit obsolete. So I might rework this weapon in the future, depending on player feedback.


[b]MRL10 rebalance[/b]
The MRL10 has been updated to feel more like a proper piece of mobile light artillery.
- Rockets have distance fuze
- Damage: 30 -> 60
- Reload time: 4 -> 8
- Increased destruction radius: 1 -> 2.5
- Increased recoil


[b]Collision damage[/b]
[i]Why does the bigger mech not simply eat the smaller mech?[/i] Well, now they can!
You can now deal collision damage to other vehicles by ramming into them. The total damage is calculated based on the mass difference and relative velocity. With it being impossible to deal damage to vehicles that are heavier/bigger than your own. 

Long story short: the Wojtech can now damage quite a few opponents, simply by walking into them.


[b]Destruction improvements[/b]
Similar to the collision damage system, it is now possible to damage walls and windows by colliding with them. With the destructive force being calculated based on your vehicle weight and speed.
Additionally, walls now have a "crumble" mechanic. Where voxels, that aren't connected to enough other voxels, will slowly crumble away.


[b]Mech speed increase[/b]
All mechs got some much needed engine maintenance, making them a bit faster than before.

L1A1
Engine force: 20000 -> 30000

Badger
Engine force: 9500 -> 11000

HEV-E
Engine force: 18000 -> 23000

Wojtech
Engine force: 65000 -> 72500


[b]Updated tech-tree layout[/b]
The departments of Combat and Demolition got some restructuring. This is to make room for some future planned unlockables. But also to improve the overall unlock progression, especially for the department of Demolition. 


[b]Enemy spawn system[/b]
The enemy spawning system got some tweaks.
-It's now a bit smarter, also keeping in mind where you have been, as to not spawn enemies directly behind you.
-Mission difficulty now has a bigger impact on the respawn rate.
-The demolition charge spider bot units should spawn a bit less.
-It should now generally rely more on sending reinforcements from other places on the map, instead of respawning units close to the player.


[b]Other[/b]
-There is now an option to control mechs with tank controls. This way, you can control their lower body and torso separately. Definitely the more difficult way of playing, as the torso of most mechs have a fairly constricted turn radius. But I have been enjoying so far!
-There are now separate optional key-bindings for firing weapon 3 & 4
-General effect improvements
-The HMG & HMG-Twin can now do minor destruction

notes.title: Update 0.1.7.2
notes.content:
Just a quick patch bringing in some minor improvements.

[h3]Improvements[/h3]
-Fixed key rebindings not saving. Somehow this issue had returned. Let's hope it stays gone permanently this time.
-Improved missile controllability. 
-Swapped reverse steering for wheeled vehicles. Added option in settings menu to revert to how it used to work.

[b]Hovertank[/b]
-Reverted back to mech control scheme
-Made weapon hard points more versatile, allowing for more weapon types
-Reduced health to compensate for improved versatility and ease of control

notes.title: Update 0.1.7.1: Feedback Valentine
notes.content:
Based on gathered feedback from the past week, I have made this initial small patch with some minor improvements, bug fixes and weapon rebalancing. Expect more updates in the near future, and let me know if you run into any problems.

[h3]Small improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] There is now a basic vehicle direction indicator for both Tanks and Wheeled vehicles. This can be toggled in the options menu. This is the first iteration, and will be improved upon in the future.
[*] It has been made a bit clearer what the status of a research note is (Available, Unlocked, Locked)
[*] Collected resources text is now outlined to the left
[*] Frozen Fire enemy unit count has been decreased. As this mission had a larger difficulty spike than intended.
[/list]

[h3]Bug fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Key rebindings are now properly saved
[*] You will now keep your resources when you choose to "replay" a mission, instead of returning to base
[*] Resolution drop-down menu scrolling fixed
[*] Minor grammar fixes.
[/list]

[h3]Weapon/Support rebalancing[/h3]
Quite a few buffs, mainly in the department of demolition. But also some minor nerfs for the laser weapons and deployable turrets. 

[b]Breacher[/b]
[list] [*] Damage: 2 -> 3
[*] Pellet count: 8 -> 12
[*] Min spread: 2 -> 1.5
[*] Max spread: 4 -> 8
[*] Reload time: 2 -> 4
[/list]
[b]rpg[/b]
[list]
[*] Damage: 90  -> 75
[*] Radius: 2.5 -> 6
[/list]
[b]MML8 + Flanker 6x2[/b]
[list]
[*] Damage: 25 -> 35
[/list]
[b]MRL10[/b]
[list]
[*] Damage: 25 -> 30
[*] Radius: 2 -> 3.5
[/list]
[b]GL20 + GL40[/b]
[list]
[*] Radius: 2.5 -> 4
[/list]
[b]Cluster Launcher[/b]
[list]
[*] Bomblet damage: 7 -> 10
[/list]
[b]L-16[/b]
[list]
[*] Reload time: 1.25 -> 1.5
[/list]
[b]L-8x2[/b]
[list]
[*] Reload time: 1 -> 1.5
[/list][i]These 2 laser weapons were proving to be very effective. An increase in their reload time should allow them to keep their powerful burst damage, while also making other options more viable[/i]

[b]PL-L[/b]
[list]
[*] Damage: 20 -> 32
[*] Reload time: 1 -> 1.1
[/list]
[b]MG Turret[/b]
[list]
[*] Spread: 1 -> 2
[*] Attack distance: 120 -> 80
[/list]
[b]HMG Turret[/b]
[list]
[*] Spread: 1 -> 2
[*] Attack distance: 120 -> 90
[/list]
[b]Laser Turret[/b]
[list]
[*] Spread: 3 -> 1
[*] Attack distance: 120 -> 70
[/list][i]Turrets don't have a time or ammo limit. Combining this with a long attack range made them very powerful. These changes should still make it viable to build turret based kill-zones. But also give the enemy a fighting change.[/i]

notes.title: Update 0.1.7.0: Demo Day
notes.content:
[b]Mission 7: Artillery Town[/b]
Added mission 7. A fairly straightforward and simple mission set in the Town environment

[b]DEMO Unit[/b]
Buffed plasma cannon range
Fixed pathfinding and LOS check
Updated map layout

[b]Tech-Tree[/b]
You can now view items further in the Tech-Tree, making it easier to plan-ahead

[b]Explosions[/b]
Decreased damage fall-off of all explosions

[b]AMR[/b]
Increased fire rate
Increased max spread
	This is to differentiate it more from the Gauss Rifle, as they both fullfill a similar role.
	Carefull shooting is still required for long-range accuracy.
	But you can now go into full-auto "panic mode", making the AMR more usefull at closer ranges.

[b]AC-20[/b]
Increased fire-rate slightly

[b]AC-20 HB[/b]
Decreased max spread

[b]Other[/b]
Gave most objectives unique icons
Lighting tweaks, mainly on Town maps
HIVE Generators (those glowy things) now give a small salvage reward upon destruction

notes.title: Preparing the upcoming Demo - DevInside 03
notes.content:
First off, I'd like to thank everyone who checked out the playtest! All the gathered feedback will play a role in shaping the future of Mech Havoc.

[hr][/hr] 
[h2]Upcoming Demo[/h2]
The next major milestone for Mech Havoc is the upcoming demo release, scheduled for early February.

This demo will feature new content, mainly in the form of 2 new missions. One of these missions introduces a new HIVE prototype unit to defeat: the [i]Demolitions Engineering and Matériel Ordinance Unit[/i], or DEMO Unit for short. In addition, the demo will feature rebalancing and improvements based on your feedback.

[hr][/hr] 
[h2]Roadmap[/h2]
Based on player feedback, I’ve outlined a list of planned updates and features, organized into three groups based on when I intend to implement them. Please note that all plans are subject to change.

[h3]Demo release[/h3]
[i]Updates planned for the upcoming demo release:[/i]
[list]
[*] [b]2 new missions[/b]. One mission features the new "DEMO Unit."
[*] [b]Improved visibility/color tweaking[/b]. While the "nighttime" aesthetic is intentional, many playtesters reported poor visibility, so this will be addressed.
[*] [b]Updated music[/b].
[*] [b]Balancing tweaks[/b].
[/list]
[h3]Post-Demo release[/h3]
[i]Features that will be prioritized after the demo release:[/i]
[list]
[*] [b]Ramming damage![/b]
[*] [b]Arching/indirect fire weapons[/b]. This feature will be added to the grenade weapons.
[*] [b]Mech control options[/b]. Provide an option to control mechs using tank controls.
[*] [b]Vehicle direction indicator[/b].
[*] [b]More mission types[/b]. Thanks to your suggestions, I’ve got some great ideas for additional mission types.
[/list]
[h3]Future[/h3]
[i]Planned features that will take longer to implement, for which I can't guarantee a timeline:[/i]
[list]
[*] [b]An endless/roguelike/survival mode[/b]. One of the most requested features! If you have any suggestions on how this could take shape, let me know!
[*] [b]Differentiate the vehicles more[/b]. Possibly by adding passive abilities to vehicles.
[*] [b]AI Buddies[/b]. AI-controlled units like drones or mechs that fight alongside you.
[/list]

notes.title: Weapons! - DevInside 02
notes.content:
[h2][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45217977/2d3ca84d83005d6f147b440edf410e3e1d69349b.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45217977/f580439efad02cfb5e370e670ca58827f28adc2e.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45217977/b3d93af6ebbca21647cabd869ffb632915eb7a11.png[/img] Weapons![/h2]
Arguably the most essential tool for taking on a horde of evil robots! In Mech Havoc, you’ll have access to an extensive arsenal, with each weapon categorized into one of three main types. Let’s dive into these categories and take a closer look at some of the powerful tools you can wield in Mech Havoc!

[h2][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45217977/2d3ca84d83005d6f147b440edf410e3e1d69349b.png[/img] Ballistic Weapons[/h2]
[i]Your bread and butter. [/i]

This category combines simplicity with versatility, offering a wide range of reliable, hard-hitting options. Ballistic weapons may be the more traditional choice, but their effectiveness and adaptability make them essential tools in any arsenal. From high-caliber machine guns to precise sniper rifles, this category has something for every combat scenario.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45217977/6ee8780c8e5ee92708b278ca8693efb862cb0af6.gif[/img]

[b]Twin HMG[/b]
Do you like heavy machine guns? What if we stick 2 of them together? Then you end up with the Twin HMG! With a large magazine, solid damage output, and a highly efficient fire rate, this weapon is built for reliability in nearly any encounter.

[b]Cluster Launcher[/b]
A powerful single-shot grenade launcher that fires high-caliber cluster grenades. Upon detonation, each grenade releases a swarm of 16 smaller explosives that cover a broad area. Perfect for clearing groups of enemies.

[b]RCL-Beehive[/b]
A recoilless rifle that fires specialized shells, inspired by the real-world "Beehive" design. These shells release a swarm of flechettes mid-flight, saturating a wide area with projectiles. It takes up to half a second for all the flechettes to be ejected. Making the weapon especially effective for crowd control at longer ranges.

[h2][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45217977/f580439efad02cfb5e370e670ca58827f28adc2e.png[/img] Rocket Weapons[/h2]
[i]Missiles! Rockets! EXPLOSIONS![/i]

As the name suggests, this category is packed with rocket and missile-based weaponry, giving you an array of powerful options for delivering explosive devastation directly to your foes! If you're a fan of explosions and destruction, this category is made for you!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45217977/eab85e8872ef1dbc9a2ce131c4369069a35ebb2a.gif[/img]

[b]RPG[/b]
Your starting rocket launcher. Fires a single unguided rocket that's capable of dealing a decent amount of damage. While it’s a straightforward, no-frills option, its effectiveness makes it a reliable choice.

[b]MRL10[/b]
Unguided rocket artillery. Fires a volley of up to 10 rockets with a wide spread. While it’s built for area destruction, controlled bursts can improve accuracy, allowing for more targeted strikes when needed. Perfect for overwhelming groups of enemies. Especially if you unlock the later variants, like the MRL20 and MRL30.

[b]Flanker 6x2[/b]
Similar to the MRL10, but instead launches up to 12 guided missiles at a 45° angle. This unique firing trajectory, paired with a precise guidance system, allows you to target enemies in otherwise hard-to-reach locations.

[h2][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45217977/b3d93af6ebbca21647cabd869ffb632915eb7a11.png[/img] Experimental Weapons[/h2]
[i]Hight-tech destruction[/i]

This high-tech category features some of the most sophisticated and cutting-edge weaponry available, including lasers, plasma cannons, railguns, and more. Ideal for those who prefer futuristic firepower, this category offers options for effortlessly slicing through armor, striking at long range, and neutralizing enemies with high-efficiency energy-based attacks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45217977/371e524e167dfbf7d04aab168c1dd73ba8998ea8.gif[/img]

[b]L-16[/b]
What's a sci-fi shooter without laser weapons? Designed for rapid-fire precision, the L-16 fires a series of short-pulse lasers with minimal recoil. Additionally, like most laser weapons in Mech Havoc, its accuracy improves with sustained fire.

[b]BEAM[/b]
Build on the same laser technology as the L-16, the BEAM instead fires a continuous and pinpoint accurate beam of energy. Perfect for targeting enemy weak spots.

[b]PL-Grenadier[/b]
The Plasma Launcher - Grenadier variant: The result of an effort to explore plasma-based grenade technology. Plasma weapons are especially effective against armored targets, easily destroying reinforced parts that would pose a challenge for conventional weaponry.

notes.title: Mech Havoc Announced! - DevInside 01
notes.content:
The Mech Havoc steam page has now been life for about 1 week. The perfect moment to publish the first official DevInside! These DevInsides are intended to give more inside into the development of Mech Havoc.

A new DevInside will be posted about once a month. These posts will be about the current development progress of Mech Havoc, some insides into game mechanics and upcoming playtests.


[h3]Play tests[/h3]
Talking about playtests. Right now there is no public build of Mech Havoc. However, i intend to fix this as soon as possible! The plan is to have a playtest before the end of this year. More information about this will be shared at a later date.

[h3]That's it![/h3]
For now i don't have any other exciting news to share. So, uh, have this gif of a hover tank getting blown up by a rocket! 🚀
